title: CS 104: Course Info
description: Fridays will be designated for lab sections, and give you an opportunity to practice what you learned in the Monday and Wednesday lectures. There will be 8 weekly lab exercises that are to be completed in the lab section. All lab exercises will be submitted on Gradescope. We expect these lab exercises be completed during lab time. We also strongly recommend you come to class, especially for some of the later lab sections which have pair exercises and require access to in-class resources that will be taken down at the end of lab section. There will be 8 weekly assignments for the course as well as a final project. * Each weekly assignment (1 thru 8) is worth 8 points. * Each weekly lab writeup is worth 2 points. title: Game Theory and Mechanism Design
description: # Game Theory and Mechanism Design. The main objective of this course is to introduce the fundamental tools of game theory and a few equilibrium concepts. During this course, we will also look at applications from a variety of disciplines and delve into some of the fascinating mathematics that underlies game theory. This course begins with an introduction into Game Theory. It then introduces strategic and extensive form games, and games with societal aspects to them. \*\*Extensive form games: \*\*Definition, examples, games of imperfect information, games of incomplete information, repeated games, the folk theorem of average payoffs, Nash equilibrium in repeated games with average payoff (7 lectures). **Cooperative games:** Transferable utility games, the core, the Shapley value, Nash bargaining (5 lectures). 3. be able to explain precisely, and apply solution concepts to examples of games. 4. be able to apply the mathematical concepts discussed over the duration of the course. | Course Title | Game Theory and Mechanism Design |.
